Element.attribute: Define business cutover and deployment approach

Development and execution of a realistic cutover and deployment approach is a critical activity to confirm that the enhanced capabilities, processes and tools are established successfully. The approach will drive realization of benefits, enable the program to maintain an appropriate level of visibility and momentum, and determine the level of risk inherent in the upcoming transition.

When building the approach, it is important to: 

  • Align the approach to all components of the organization’s operating model to clarify when changes will be implemented and determine how changes made later in the timeline can be rolled out to business units or countries that have already been transitioned. 
  • Draw on the expertise within the business and technology teams to validate the feasibility of the transition approach and the subsequent detailed transition plan.
  • Manage the program as an integrated set of projects, in order to better manage dependencies. 
  • Consider all stakeholders and outline how each will be engaged in transition activities throughout the project. 
  • Fully train stakeholders in transition activities overall and individually-assigned area of responsibility. 
  • Have business and IT managers fully engaged with stakeholders throughout the transition period.
  • Include a high level communications plan that outlines the appropriate communication mechanisms and messaging levels for each target audience. 
  • Focus on the areas where overruns or higher costs can occur, such as systems and interface development, scope change, recruitment, site set-up, level of clean-up needed and knowledge transfer.

The cutover and deployment approach provides a high-level overview of changes that will result from introduction of a new solution and how the organization will manage through the transition to new capabilities, processes and tools. It describes the resulting changes, and how the changes will affect roles and responsibilities within the organization. The business cutover and deployment approach presents possible options for conducting the transition, outlines a high-level timeline, and includes an overview of the transition governance structure and processes.

Defining the business approach encompasses functional and organizational aspects of the cutover and deployment. (The organization’s approach for application, data and technology infrastructure transition aspects are captured and documented in a separate section of the approach document. The two sections work in tandem and are the basis for a more detailed cutover and deployment plan.)

The business approach outlines the preparations for managing the organization and process aspects of the cutover and deployment. It includes: 

  • Technology team touch points and contacts, to enable communication and teamwork 
  • Business readiness management, to confirm accountabilities and governance 
  • Change impact analysis, to confirm stakeholders and impacts 
  • Procedures, to confirm alignment of current and future business processes 
  • Training and development, to confirm that staff can be educated on future process organization design, to confirm that future processes can be staffed and managed
  • Talent management, to confirm plans to manage future staff and resource needs 
  • Deployment and post-go-live support, to confirm plans for cutover and future business continuity

These additional business concerns should also be considered when drafting the approach: 

  • The organization’s change history and lessons learned from previous transitions 
  • The organization’s commitment to building or maintaining a continuous improvement capability
  • Alignment of the new solution to organization and program strategy 
  • The stakeholders and resources who will have a role in transition activities 
  • Training that will be required 
  • The level of complexity within each business unit or country that could require longer lead times due to legislation, labor situations, complexity or level of effort 
  • The budget available and level of investment required for each option
